title: The AI Ledger
introduction: New reporting week, reviewed through November 16 at 20:00 UTC. Qwen4-Max leads; OpenAI adds a specialized moderation classifier, while Codex activity remains prerelease. The complete November 9–15 issue is preserved unchanged. Two prior forecasts remain pending through November 22; two new forecasts target the following week or its explicit end deadline. No new timing rumor met the evidence threshold. Confidence labels are qualitative, never probabilities.

items.title: Qwen4-Max launches beyond the separate preview
items.summary: QwenCloud lists qwen4-max for multimodal reasoning, coding and agent tasks, with tool calling, structured outputs, explicit caching and reasoning summaries. The specifications list a one-million-token context window and pay-as-you-go access.
items.whyItMatters: A new hosted candidate for long-context agent evaluations. Test compatibility and costs on your workload; this is not evidence of local weight availability or benchmark superiority.
items.confidenceReason: Official publisher sources support the announcement. Capabilities have not been independently tested for this newsletter.
items.historicalContext: The November 11 qwen4-max-preview was a distinct Token Plan preview. Today’s dated entry uses qwen4-max; do not count the preview and launch as two unrelated model families.

items.title: OpenAI adds a specialized image-safety classifier
items.summary: Approved organizations can use omni-moderation-csam-latest through the moderation API without charge. It supplies distinct signals for possible child sexual abuse material and possible AI-generated CSAM to prioritize human review.
items.whyItMatters: Relevant to eligible trust-and-safety teams, not a coding-model upgrade. A classifier signal is not a definitive judgment and does not replace review.
items.confidenceReason: Official publisher sources support the announcement. Capabilities have not been independently tested for this newsletter.
items.historicalContext: This is a specialized moderation release, separate from OpenAI’s general-purpose GPT and coding models.

items.title: Codex 0.171 remains in prerelease
items.summary: The official repository published 0.171.0-alpha.9 on November 16. Its brief release note does not document a feature set. The latest stable release observed remains 0.169.0 from November 13.
items.whyItMatters: Do not treat an alpha artifact as a stable rollout or infer new model support from the version number. Existing stable users need not switch solely because an alpha exists.
items.confidenceReason: Official publisher sources support the announcement. Capabilities have not been independently tested for this newsletter.
items.historicalContext: The prior weekly edition covered 0.169.0. Today’s alpha is new evidence of release activity, not a verified new stable feature.

items.title: Carry-over forecast · November 16–22: control updates from two harness publishers
items.summary: We expect at least two of Codex, Claude Code, Copilot CLI and OpenCode to publish stable releases that add or fix permission, background-task or session-control behavior during the next calendar week.
items.whyItMatters: Cross-publisher progress would be stronger evidence of an operational-controls trend than another isolated patch.
items.confidenceReason: Recent releases support the direction, but the count and timing are editorial forecasts, not publisher commitments or calculated probabilities.
items.historicalContext: The November 9 and November 10 follow-up forecasts each required only one release and were met. This prospectively raises the threshold to two distinct harnesses and excludes the current week.

items.resolutionCriteria: Pass if official stable releases from at least two distinct named harnesses have published_at dates from November 16 through November 22 and explicitly document a permission, background-task or session-control addition or fix. Count each harness once. Prereleases, documentation-only changes and model support alone do not count. Otherwise fail at 23:59 UTC November 22.
items.counterarguments: Recent patches may reduce immediate demand, releases may cluster before the window, or work may stay in prerelease.

items.historicalContext: The launch separates broad Fable access from direct Mythos access. Task-specific Claude Security access is outside this forecast.

charts.title: Qwen4-Max: documented token ceilings
charts.description: Provider specifications checked November 16. These are distinct output budgets, not benchmark scores.
charts.selectionCriteria: Compare the documented non-thinking output limit with the combined thinking-plus-final-answer limit for the same model.
charts.caveat: The larger budget includes reasoning tokens, so it is not a promise of twice as much visible output. Context, input budgets and API settings also constrain requests. Rolling documentation observation date, not independent performance measurement.
